clue.text: Charged boundary with pick and staple to secure cold bog

parts.note: to pick is to elect or choose

indicators.note: the staple food holds the next pieces fast inside it, as if securing them

parts.note: rice is a staple food
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a fen is a marsh or bog

explanation.surface: Someone builds a fence round a cold marsh using a pick and staples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staple' looks like a wire fastener but it is a staple food; RICE takes C and FEN inside, giving RI+CFEN+CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire carrying current makes a barrier that is literally charged, keeping livestock in a field.

clue.text: French evangelist with cattle on ship making fortune

parts.note: the gospel writer Luke is Luc in French
kine is an old plural for cows
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A French gospel writer sails with a herd of cows and gets rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Good fortune is the state of being lucky; both nouns name chance going your way.

clue.text: Bum finds penny in prison

indicators.note: the penny sits inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny (from Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: A tramp in jail turns up a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' is a verb here, meaning to scrounge, not the noun for a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum a cigarette is to beg or scrounge it from someone, the same as to sponge.

clue.text: Gods of victory and war mostly overturned dish

indicators.note: in a down light, overturned means the combined pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Nike is the Greek goddess of victory

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war

explanation.surface: Classical deities of victory and war knock over a serving dish.
explanation.walkthrough: NIKE plus MAR (Mars with 'mostly' trimming its end) gives NIKEMAR, which 'overturned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round ovenproof bowl for baking individual portions is a kind of dish.

clue.text: Drink tea with endless delight

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: bliss is great delight

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a cup of tea with unending pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry white Burgundy wine is a drink, named after the French town where it is made.

clue.text: Bomb in with a will (but without limits) to cafe

indicators.note: the bomb goes in the trimmed word
without limits means the first and last letters are lost

parts.note: someone who dies with a will in place is testate
a mine is an explosive device, a bomb

explanation.surface: Someone hurries eagerly to a cafe with a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a will' looks like 'eagerly' but means having made a will: TESTATE, which 'without limits' trims to ESTAT, holding MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small French bar or cafe selling drinks, a borrowing from French.

clue.text: Jessica dizzily drinking port

indicators.note: the outer words are drinking, that is taking in, the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: Jessica gets tipsy on port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink, but it is a harbour town in southern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: This Andalusian city is an ancient seaport on the Atlantic coast of Spain.

clue.text: Magic Parmesan recipe for political skulduggery

indicators.note: a recipe is a way of mixing ingredients, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cookery note recommends cheese as a wondrous ingredient in some dirty politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading damaging stories about a rival is underhand political trickery.

clue.text: Blue door curiously concealing crush — stress may increase it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hide the next word inside them
curiously means arranged in an odd way

parts.note: to press is to crush

explanation.surface: A strangely painted door hides a crowd crushing behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: 'stress may increase it' describes the answer rather than naming a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety and tension are known to raise the force of circulating blood on artery walls.

clue.text: Scholar spooks patriarch hidden in nut tree

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree

indicators.note: the patriarch is hidden in the spooks' letters

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency, spooks being spies
Adam is the first patriarch in Genesis

explanation.surface: An academic frightens an old patriarch who is lurking in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooks' is a noun, the spies of the CIA, not a verb for scaring.
explanation.definitionFit: An Australian evergreen whose rich round kernels are sold as nuts.

clue.text: Young man with it, turning, ebbing and flowing

indicators.note: turning means the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A trendy young man changes direction like the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that ebbs and flows rises and falls with the moon's pull on the sea.

clue.text: Assistant catching second stage whisper

indicators.note: the assistant catches, that is holds inside, the next piece

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A helper overhears a quiet remark at the theatre for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark an actor makes to the audience, unheard by the other characters, is a theatrical whisper.

clue.text: Instrument welcoming holy man to US city

indicators.note: the instrument welcomes the holy man inside it

parts.note: a kazoo is a humming musical instrument
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A band greets a visiting monk to an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: This Michigan city is known in songs and in the name of a once-famous filing-systems company.

clue.text: Degrade pile penetrating scent's centre

indicators.note: the pile goes inside the central letters
centre means the inner letters with the ends dropped

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A pile of something has got into the heart of a perfume and spoilt it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' here keeps all but the outer letters of the five-letter word, not just its single middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower the worth or dignity of something is to debase it or make it less valued.

clue.text: Butterfly catcher with clipper gaining weight?

indicators.note: gaining says the next piece is added on

parts.note: one who pinks cloth, cutting a zigzag edge, is a pinker
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A lepidopterist with shears seems to be putting on pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butterfly' is Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly; its naval officer seduces and abandons the heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Puccini's opera the American lieutenant wins the heroine nicknamed Butterfly, so he is her catcher.

clue.text: Hot spot for Puritans dropping one off

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is left out of the word
off indicates the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Strict Puritans lose one of their number on the way to somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: PURITANS without its I leaves PURTANS, which 'off' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered sunny place that catches and holds heat is a warm spot.

clue.text: Boxer, maybe, with electronic phone featured in retrograde film genre

indicators.note: these pieces are featured inside the turned film genre
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: noir is a dark film genre
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
a bell is slang for a phone call, as in give me a bell

explanation.surface: A boxer appears with an electronic phone in an old-fashioned film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' is not a fighter but the 1900 Chinese uprising, an example of an armed revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boxer uprising in China was an armed revolt against foreign influence.

clue.text: Mother hedgehog belonging to "boys only" club?

parts.note: ma is mother
Sonic is the video game hedgehog

explanation.surface: Mum and a cartoon hedgehog try to join a men-only club.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasonry is traditionally a male-only fraternity, so its lodges are a club just for boys.

clue.text: Animals getting a bone circle copper-plated

indicators.note: the copper is plated round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rib is a bone
O is a circle

explanation.surface: Some creatures receive a copper-plated bone ring.
explanation.definitionFit: North American reindeer are large deer; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Unruly teen absorbing reflux in African town

indicators.note: the rearranged letters absorb the next piece
unruly means disorderly, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: the ebb is the tide flowing back, a reflux

explanation.surface: A wild teenager suffers acid reflux in a town in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflux' looks medical but means the tide flowing back out, its ebb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ugandan town on Lake Victoria, known for its airport and a famous 1976 hostage rescue.

clue.text: Doleful, the Spanish setter interrupts rising composer

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: the setter interrupts the turned composer by going inside
in a down light rising means read upwards

parts.note: John Cage was an American composer
a crossword setter refers to themselves as I

explanation.surface: A doleful compiler interrupts a composer on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer is John Cage; 'rising' suits a down light, where his name reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mournful, lamenting the dead, as in a lament or funeral poem.

clue.text: First bit of evening paper let loose by fruit-bearer

indicators.note: loose means let free and disordered, so these letters are rearranged
the first bit of the word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An evening newspaper is set free by someone carrying fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists E first but it falls at the end, after the rearranged PAPER LET.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard plant that produces pomes each autumn bears fruit.

clue.text: Allegedly nosey sort of churchman

indicators.note: allegedly means as it is said, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a prier is someone who pries, a nosey person

explanation.surface: A cleric supposedly pokes his nose into things.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a priory, ranking below an abbot, is a monastic churchman.

clue.text: Expression of regret about time range

indicators.note: the expression of regret goes about the next piece

parts.note: alas expresses regret

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over time running out, or over a range of options.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain range of north-west Africa, stretching across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

clue.text: Startle, Madagascar-style?

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
RM is the international vehicle code for Madagascar

explanation.surface: Something done in the manner of the Madagascar island might give you a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madagascar-style' reads in reverse: the style piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten or put on edge suddenly, as a warning bell does.

clue.text: What's to be ground by King George I?

parts.note: GR, Georgius Rex, is the royal cipher of King George
the regnal numeral I means first, abbreviated 1st

explanation.surface: A riddle asks what a king of England would grind.
explanation.walkthrough: George I would be written GR 1st, the numeral giving the I-S-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn brought to the mill for grinding; from the proverb 'all is grist to the mill'.

clue.text: Officer finding one sort of fly in pipe

indicators.note: the fly and one go in the pipe

parts.note: a brier (briar) is a tobacco pipe made from heath root
a gad is a gadfly, a biting fly
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A soldier discovers an insect stuck in his pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army rank commanding a brigade, between colonel and major general.

clue.text: Part of speech with which to make firm declaration

parts.note: a pronoun is a grammatical part of speech
to cement is to make firm or secure

explanation.surface: A speech is analysed for words that could firm up a statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' seems to be the definition but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal public statement or announcement is an official proclamation.
